why: `unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void) -> u8` -- the FFI-shaped callback, so C, C++ and Rust all drive ONE state machine implementation. **rclrs 0.5.1 has no lifecycle support whatsoever** -- the whole stage reports zero theirs-only rows in the Rust lane -- so every item here is an extension by definition. The RTOS scenario is REP-2002 itself: a device that owns hardware needs a supervisor-driven `configure`/`activate`/`deactivate` protocol so an actuator can be brought up and parked without restarting the image, and `ros2 lifecycle set` is how the rest of the graph asks for it. We implement the state machine once in `nros_core::lifecycle` and surface it in all three languages. NOTE this alias is the source of the C-header defect recorded on `c:lifecycle_register_on_configure`: `Option<LifecycleCallbackFnCtx>` reaches the C ABI as `struct Option_LifecycleCallbackFnCtx`.
